title: No Matter How I Look at It, It's You Guys' Fault I'm Not Popular!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Tomoko Kuroki, a socially anxious otaku who thinks dating games have made her an expert, starts high school expecting popularity and finds she can barely talk to anyone. Early chapters are cringe comedy built on her awkward schemes, crude fantasies and harsh inner monologue. As the long-running series goes on, Tomoko slowly gains friends and the manga becomes an ensemble story about growing up, with hints of romance between the girls.
life_message: Even someone stuck in loneliness and self-sabotage can grow into friendship, one awkward step at a time.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Tomoko stews over slights in her head but seldom retaliates; worth found in acceptance.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Little pressure to conform is endorsed; quirks accepted by friends.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Classmate friendships replace family as the main support.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: School cliques satirized; friends meet as equals.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Pop culture and school life; no faith or custom.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Being accepted as oneself is the long arc.

folkways.japan: Fear of standing out, school clique hierarchy and the hikikomori phenomenon reflect Japanese social pressures the series satirizes.

delivery.evidence: No source comments on delivery; summaries show the outlook carried by plot and character choices (to verify).
delivery.note: Its outlook on loneliness and belonging is carried by satire and Tomoko's slow growth rather than stated lessons.

winners_losers: Tomoko and her growing circle win; isolation and otaku self-delusion lose. Sympathy goes to the socially awkward.
